t:
The Naval Reserve Act of 1938 (52 Stat. 1175), as amended, is hereby further amended by adding after section 508 thereof an additional title as follows:


“TITLE VI—
NURSE CORPS RESERVE

“Sec. 601. 
A Nurse Corps Reserve is hereby established which shall be a branch of the Naval Reserve and shall be administered under the same provisions in all respects (except as may be necessary to adapt said provisions to the Nurse Corps Reserve, or as specifically provided herein) as those contained in this Act or which may hereafter be enacted with respect to the Volunteer Reserve.


“Sec. 602. 
Members of the Nurse Corps Reserve may be commissioned in appropriate ranks corresponding to those of the Nurse Corps of the Regular Navy in accordance with such regulations as the Secretary of the Navy may prescribe. Such members of the Nurse Corps Reserve, when on active duty, shall have the same authority in and about naval hospitals and other activities of the Medical Department of the Navy as officers of the Nurse Corps of the Regular Navy.


“Sec. 603. 
The Reserve established by this title shall be composed of members who are female citizens of the United States and who shall have such professional or other qualifications as shall be prescribed by the Secretary of the Navy.


“Sec. 604. 
All nurses of the Volunteer Reserve appointed under the authority of title 1, section 4, of this Act are hereby transferred to the Nurse Corps Reserve established by section 601 of this title in such permanent ranks as the Secretary of the Navy may determine and the temporary ranks held by those on active duty on the effective date of this title shall not be vacated by reason of such transfer. Each nurse so transferred, who at the time of such transfer had to her credit leave accrued but not taken, may, subsequent to such transfer, be granted such leave without loss of pay and allowances.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is purely internal military personnel administration with no outside party, which would be "No". But the section authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to prescribe regulations governing commissioning, and under the definition and the worked example on regulatory authority, a grant of rulemaking authority counts as participation even when discretionary. The call is uncertain because military personnel regulations rarely involve public comment in practice.
fable.s: Members of the Nurse Corps Reserve may be commissioned in appropriate ranks corresponding to those of the Nurse Corps of the Regular Navy in accordance with such regulations as the Secretary of the Navy may prescribe.

qwen_block.w: This section establishes a new branch of the military (the Nurse Corps Reserve) and defines its membership and administration. It does not involve consultation with or participation by people outside the federal government in decision-making. The members are federal employees/officers, and the regulations are prescribed by the Secretary of the Navy. There is no advisory board, public comment period, or coordination with external entities described.
qwen_block.s: A Nurse Corps Reserve is hereby established which shall be a branch of the Naval Reserve and shall be administered under the same provisions in all respects... as those contained in this Act or which may hereafter be enacted with respect to the Volunteer Reserve.

opus.w: The section lets the Secretary of the Navy prescribe regulations for commissioning Nurse Corps Reserve members. Under the DEFINITION, requiring or authorizing rulemaking counts as participation, and Example 6 shows that a permissive grant ('may by regulation') is enough. The opposite reading treats this as internal military administration with no outside parties, but the labeling rules treat a grant of rulemaking authority as participation in itself. The military-affairs exemption from notice-and-comment adds some uncertainty.
opus.s: Members of the Nurse Corps Reserve may be commissioned in appropriate ranks corresponding to those of the Nurse Corps of the Regular Navy in accordance with such regulations as the Secretary of the Navy may prescribe.
opus.b: 1. **The tempting reading.** This looks like a purely internal military personnel provision: setting up the Nurse Corps Reserve, giving ranks, and transferring nurses. Everyone involved seems to be inside the federal government, which would make the answer "No." Military personnel rules are also exempt from notice-and-comment under the APA. But the DEFINITION and Example 6 say that any grant of authority to issue regulations counts as participation, even when the agency may choose not to use it ("may"). Section 602 grants that kind of authority.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes the Nurse Corps Reserve and sets internal administrative rules for its membership, such as qualifications prescribed by the Secretary of the Navy. It does not require the federal government to consult or coordinate with people outside the government (such as states, tribes, or the general public) before making a decision. The process described is essentially an application for military service, which falls under the exclusion for 'applications for benefits or grants' and does not constitute participation in the decision-making process as defined.
qwen_chat.s:
“Sec. 603. 
The Reserve established by this title shall be composed of members who are female citizens of the United States and who shall have such professional or other qualifications as shall be prescribed by the Secretary of the Navy.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Secretary of the Navy prescribes regulations for qualifications and ranks, this involves some form of administrative process that could be construed as participation. However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and setting qualification standards for military service is an internal administrative function, not a consultation with outside parties. The text describes the establishment of a military reserve branch and the internal administrative rules for its members (who are federal employees/officers when on active duty). There is no mention of consulting with states, tribes, the public, or outside experts before making decisions. The "participation" here is limited to individuals applying to join the military, which is an application for a position/benefit, not participation in a federal decision-making process as defined.
